subject: Biology
description: Photosynthesis, plant hormones, transport systems, classification

questions.stem: The GREEN PIGMENT in plants that absorbs sunlight for photosynthesis is:
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll-a and chlorophyll-b are the main photosynthetic pigments, located in chloroplasts. They absorb mainly blue (430 nm) and red (660 nm) light, reflecting green — hence the colour. Carotene and xanthophyll are accessory pigments (yellow-orange). Anthocyanin gives red/purple colours to fruits and autumn leaves.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The process by which plants lose WATER VAPOUR through stomata is called:
questions.explanation: Transpiration = evaporation of water from aerial parts (mainly through stomata on leaves). It creates a 'transpirational pull' that drives upward movement of water (ascent of sap) from roots. Translocation = movement of food through phloem. Respiration = oxidation of glucose to release ATP.

questions.stem: Match the PLANT HORMONE with its primary function. A. Auxin.  B. Gibberellin.  C. Cytokinin.  D. Abscisic acid. List-II: 1. Cell elongation; apical dominance. 2. Stem elongation; seed germination. 3. Cell division; delay senescence. 4. Stress response; seed dormancy; stomatal closure.
questions.explanation: Auxin (IAA) — cell elongation, phototropism, apical dominance. Gibberellin (GA) — stem elongation (bolting), dormancy break. Cytokinin — cell division, delays ageing. Abscisic acid (ABA) — the 'stress hormone' — closes stomata under water stress; induces seed dormancy. (Ethylene — fruit ripening.)
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The tissue in plants that conducts WATER and minerals from roots to leaves is:
questions.explanation: Xylem — unidirectional (roots → upward). Cells include tracheids and vessel elements (both dead at maturity). Phloem — bidirectional, carries organic food (sucrose) from source to sink — uses living sieve-tube elements and companion cells.

questions.stem: The overall equation of photosynthesis is:
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis: in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll, 6 CO₂ + 6 H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6 O₂. Respiration is the reverse. (The more precise form '6CO₂ + 12 H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6 O₂ + 6 H₂O' balances oxygen-labelling-experiment stoichiometry but the simpler net form is the standard textbook version.)

questions.stem: Leguminous plants (peas, beans, gram) are important because they:

options.option_text: Host nitrogen-fixing bacteria (Rhizobium) in root nodules
Produce more oxygen than other plants
Can survive without water for months

questions.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria in root nodules fix atmospheric N₂ into ammonia, enriching the soil with nitrogen. This is why legumes are used in crop rotation — they restore soil fertility naturally. Other N-fixers: Azotobacter (free-living), Cyanobacteria (e.g., Anabaena with Azolla in rice paddies).

questions.stem: The largest and smallest flowers on Earth belong to which genera, respectively?
questions.explanation: Rafflesia arnoldii (Sumatra/Borneo) has the largest single flower — up to 1 metre across, 11 kg, foul-smelling (attracts flies). Wolffia species (watermeal) are the smallest flowering plants — <1 mm. Amorphophallus titanum has the largest 'unbranched inflorescence' but not the largest single flower.
